Let $\ell\geq 2$ be a fixed constant. A graph is **$\ell K_2$-free** if it has no induced subgraph consisting of $\ell$ pairwise disjoint edges, and a graph is **$(\ell-1)$-connected** if deleting fewer than $\ell-1$ vertices leaves it connected.

**Algorithmic edge-dominating-cycle conjecture.** For every fixed $\ell\geq 2$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that finds an edge-dominating cycle in every $(\ell-1)$-connected, $\ell K_2$-free graph.

This would extend the paper’s algorithmic results beyond $2K_2$-free graphs. The provided text presents it as a proposed direction, and gives no resolution for the general fixed-$\ell$ case.

Let $G$ be a graph with a **Kempe-coloring** ${\frak C}$ of size $k$, and let a **transversal** $T$ of ${\frak C}$ contain one vertex from each color class. A **clique minor traversed by** $T$ is a clique minor whose branch sets are each traversed by $T$. **The Kempe-coloring clique-minor conjecture.** For every transversal $T$ of ${\frak C}$, there exists a clique minor traversed by $T$. The source introduces this as a common generalization of two open projects concerning Kempe-colorings and clique minors, and does not report a resolution.

Let $E$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a unitary connectivity function on $E$, and let $\mu\downarrow X$ denote the connectivity-function minor obtained by the operation defined in the source. **Finite-obstruction conjecture.** There is a finite set $S$ of connectivity functions such that, if $\mu$ is a unitary connectivity function on $E$, then $\mu$ is κ-matroidal if and only if, for every $X\subseteq E$, the connectivity function $\mu\downarrow X$ is not isomorphic to a member of $S$. This is presented as a weaker version of the preceding 4-cycle obstruction conjecture. The supplied text does not resolve whether such a finite obstruction set exists.

Let $\chi(G)$ denote the chromatic number of a graph $G$. **The weak Hedetniemi conjecture.** For every integer $n$, there exists an integer $f(n)$ such that whenever $G$ and $H$ are graphs satisfying

$$
\chi(G)\geq f(n),\qquad \chi(H)\geq f(n),
$$

one has

$$
\chi(G\times H)\geq n.
$$

This is a weaker assertion than Hedetniemi's conjecture and is introduced as relevant to the survey's discussion of adjoint functors. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

Let $\alpha_G(\lambda)$ denote the occupancy fraction of a graph $G$ in the hard-core model, and let $H_{3,8}$ be the $(3,8)$-cage, also known as the Levi graph or Tutte–Coxeter graph. **Tutte–Coxeter occupancy-fraction conjecture.** For every $3$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $7$ and every $\lambda>0$,

$$
\alpha_G(\lambda)\leq\alpha_{H_{3,8}}(\lambda).
$$

The conjecture identifies the $(3,8)$-cage as the maximizer in this girth-constrained problem and is open.

A graph $G$ is **1-unique** if, for every vertex $v$ of $G$, there is a tree-depth labeling using labels from $\{1,\dots,\operatorname{td}(G)\}$ in which $v$ is the unique vertex receiving label $1$. A graph is **critical** when it is $k$-critical for its tree-depth $k$: every proper minor has smaller tree-depth.

**Every-critical-graph conjecture.** Every critical graph is 1-unique.

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that every critical graph with tree-depth at most $4$ is 1-unique, and that critical graphs produced by certain known constructions are also 1-unique. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.

Let $G$ be a graph, let $\therefore$ denote the graph-minor relation, and let $b3(G)$ be its homological dimension. For a positive integer $d$, consider the complete graph $K_{d+2}$. **Homological dimension conjecture.** For every positive integer $d$ and graph $G$,

$$
K_{d+2}\prec G \iff \gamma(G)\geq d.
$$

The result is proved in the paper for $d=1,2,3$, detecting $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ minors; the conjecture extends this correspondence to all complete minors.

Let $F$ be a fixed strict digraph. An **$F$-subdivision** is a digraph obtained from $F$ by replacing each arc $ab$ with a directed $(a,b)$-path; the associated problem asks whether an input digraph $D$ contains an $F$-subdivision as a subdigraph. **Bang-Jensen et al.'s dichotomy conjecture.** For every digraph $F$, the $F$-subdivision problem is polynomial-time solvable or NP-complete. This conjecture concerns the algorithmic classification of fixed-digraph subdivision problems; the paper gives further support to it and, for digraphs of order four, classifies all but five exceptions.

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its spectral radius. A graph has **no $K_p$ minor** when no graph obtained from it by vertex deletions, edge deletions, and edge contractions is isomorphic to $K_p$. **McCarty's conjecture.** For every integer $p\ge3$, every graph $G$ on $n\ge p-1$ vertices with $\mu(G)\le p-2$ has at most $(p-2)n-{p-1\choose2}$ edges.

The conjecture is also recorded as an open problem and is implied by a result cited in the source. No resolution of the conjecture itself is stated.

Let $H$ and $H'$ be graphs with $m_2(H)\geq m_2(H')$. **Asymmetric Ramsey-density conjecture.** If neither $H$ nor $H'$ is a matching and at least one of $H$ or $H'$ contains a cycle, then

$$
m(F)>m_2(H,H')
$$

for every Ramsey graph $F\in R(H,H')$. This conjecture would, together with asymmetric random-Ramsey results, imply the expected Ramsey-infinite classification for unordered graph pairs containing cycles; the source gives no resolution.

A **planar graph** is a graph that can be drawn in the plane without crossings; two triangles are **adjacent** if they have at least one common edge. A graph is **4-choosable** if, for every assignment of a list of four colors to each vertex, it has a proper coloring choosing a color from each vertex's list.

**Wang–Lih conjecture.** Every planar graph without adjacent triangles is 4-choosable.

Wang and Lih proved the analogous statement for planar graphs without intersecting triangles, while the conjecture for graphs without adjacent triangles remains open. The paper studies the stronger correspondence-coloring setting, in which ordinary list coloring is generalized by allowing edge-specific matchings between color lists.

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A list assignment $L$ assigns a list of colors to each vertex; it is a $k$-assignment when $|L(v)|=k$ for every $v\in V(G)$. An equitable $L$-coloring is a proper coloring using colors from the lists such that each color appears on at most $\lceil |V(G)|/k\rceil$ vertices. The graph is equitably $k$-choosable when it has an equitable $L$-coloring for every $k$-assignment $L$.

**List Hajnál–Szemerédi conjecture.** Every graph $G$ is equitably $k$-choosable when $k\geq \Delta(G)+1$.

This is the list-coloring analogue of the Hajnál–Szemerédi theorem, which asserts equitable $k$-colorability for $k\geq\Delta(G)+1$. The source attributes the conjecture to Kostochka, West, and the third author; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

Let $s$ be an integer. An edge $\lambda$-choosable graph is a graph whose line graph is colourable from every list assignment whose list-size pattern is the partition $\lambda$. **The bounded-part edge list-colouring conjecture.** For every integer $s$, there is an integer $k(s)$ such that, whenever $k\geq k(s)$, $G$ is edge $k$-colourable, and $\lambda$ is a partition of $k$ in which every part has size at most $s$, then $G$ is edge $\lambda$-choosable. This is proposed as a weaker version of the List Colouring Conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence.

Let $G$ be a critical multigraph, meaning that $\chi'(H)<\chi'(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$, and let $m$ be an odd integer with $m\geq 3$.

**Jakobsen's bounded-order conjecture.** If

$$
\chi'(G)>\frac{m\Delta(G)+(m-3)}{m-1},
$$

then $G$ has at most $m-2$ vertices.

The source attributes this conjecture to Jakobsen and states that Andersen proved it weaker than the Goldberg–Seymour conjecture. It is therefore solved by the result established in the paper.

Let $k$ and $r$ be positive integers. A **$k$-uniform hypergraph** is a hypergraph whose edges are $k$-element subsets of its vertex set, and a **tight cycle** is a cyclically ordered sequence of vertices in which every $k$ consecutive vertices form an edge; single vertices are also regarded as tight cycles. **Gyárfás's conjecture.** There is a constant $c=c(k,r)$ such that the vertices of every $r$-edge-coloured complete $k$-uniform hypergraph can be partitioned into at most $c$ monochromatic tight cycles. The paper confirms this conjecture, so the asserted bounded partition exists for all positive integers $k$ and $r$.

For a matroid $M$, let $\d(M)$ denote its density, and call $M$ **strictly $t$-density-critical** when $d(M)>t$ while every proper minor $N$ of $M$ satisfies $d(N)\leq t$. **Finiteness conjecture.** For every $t\geq 0$, there are finitely many strictly $t$-density-critical matroids. The case $t=2$ is known from the explicit classification of the ten strictly $2$-density-critical matroids; the assertion for all $t\geq 0$ remains open.

A graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. For vertices $a$ and $b$, an $(a,b)$-path is a path with endpoints $a$ and $b$. A **Tutte path** is an $(a,b)$-path whose off-path components have at most three neighbours on the path, and a path is **maximal** if it cannot be extended while preserving the relevant path conditions.

**Claw-free Tutte-path conjecture.** For every pair of vertices $a,b$ of a connected claw-free graph, there is a maximal $(a,b)$-path which is a Tutte path.

The paper presents this as a seemingly stronger reformulation of Jackson's conjecture and proves that it is equivalent to the same open problem. Thus the assertion remains open despite the equivalence with the other formulations.

Let $M$ be a connected $k$-polymatroid and let $N$ be a connected minor of $M$. A **connected minor-preserving deletion or contraction** is a deletion or contraction that remains connected and retains $N$ as a minor. **Connectivity conjecture.** When $N \neq M$, there is an element $e$ of $E(M)-E(N)$ such that $M\backslash e$ or $M/e$ is connected and has $N$ as a minor.

The paper proves this assertion for $2$-polymatroids and suggests that the same result should hold for all $k>2$; its status is therefore unresolved in the supplied source.

A connected graph $G$ is **double-critical** if $\chi(G)=t$ and

$$
\chi\bigl(G\setminus\{x,y\}\bigr)=t-2
$$

for every edge $xy\in E(G)$. **Double-Critical Graph Conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq3$, the only double-critical $t$-chromatic graph is the complete graph $K_t$. This is the $s=2$ case of the Erdős–Lovász Tihany Conjecture and is stated as an open problem; its classification remains unresolved in general.

For positive integers $s$ and $t$, let $K^*_{s,t}$ be the complete join of $K_s$ and $\overline{K_t}$. A graph is **$K^*_{s,t}$-minor-free** if it contains no minor isomorphic to $K^*_{s,t}$. For a graph $G$ and integer $r\geqslant1$, let $\operatorname{wcol}_r(G)$ denote its weak $r$-colouring number.

**Polynomial weak colouring-number conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that for every $K^*_{s,t}$-minor-free graph $G$ and every $r\geqslant1$,

$$
\operatorname{wcol}_r(G)\leqslant f(s,t)\,r^s.
$$

The conjecture would generalise the displayed bounds for $K^*_{2,t}$- and $K^*_{3,t}$-minor-free graphs and would give polynomial weak colouring-number bounds for these minor-closed graph classes. The source gives no resolution status.
